keep: The idea is named in one line up front: a plain number saying how much of one vector lies along the other. [^1] sits on the |a||b| cos θ rule.

The picture is the brief's shadow on the line: two draggable arrows from one point, a light straight down onto b's line, both formulas read out together, the shadow shrinking to a dot at 90° and falling behind past it, then a rope and a rail, then a voltage and a current.
Worked examples computed from the rule: 3i + 4j on 4i gives 12 both ways, 3i + 4j with 4i + 3j gives 24, and the 200 N rope over 5 m gives 866.03 J.

Twelve screens alternate SHOW (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) and DO (2, 4, 6, 8, 10), ending with two mixed puzzles (11, 12). Each lesson 5 mistake in the brief has a puzzle with its own wrong pick: the answer as a vector (2, 12), sin for cos (4, 8, 11), the sign lost past 90° (4, 12), sizes multiplied without the angle (2, 10, 11).
True power is said to have the same shape as the dot product, never that it is one, as the brief requires.

The plan-drawing analogy reproduces the main result (a run's plan length is its length times cos of the slope, a vertical drop is a dot) and breaks honestly: no multiplication by a second length, and no negative lengths.
fix: Causal step skipped: the parts formula jumps from i·i = 1 and i·j = 0 to a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃. Give the chain: the rule reads the same either way round; b's parts laid nose to tail cast shadows end to end on a's line; a·i is a's shadow on the x-axis times 1, which is a₁; so b₁i gives a₁b₁.
Misconception not shown failing in the explanation: add the sizes-multiplied slip with real numbers (5 × 4 = 20 against 12) and why sin gives the wrong shadow.
Talks about the course: 'The last lesson of this topic says why that matters' in ignores. Cut it. Keep the one plain pointer that curved paths wait for Vector calculus, as the plan asks.
Vague phrase: 'only when the arrows lie together' in the mistakes. Say 'only when the arrows point the same way'.
Analogy's last sentence is muddled ('the shadow of the dot product, cast onto the floor's line'). Say the plan length is the run's shadow, the part that lies along the floor.
[^4] sits on 'So the answer has no direction', which its quote does not say. Put it on 'the dot product is a scalar, a plain number'.
whatAmILookingAt names only a₁b₁ + a₂b₂. Add a₃b₃ for the 3-D screens.
Explain's i·i line ('i and i lie together') is unclear. Say i lies along itself and is 1 long, so i·i = 1 × 1 × cos 0° = 1.
